title: WurProbe
description: One row of $RUN_DIR/probes.jsonl (STATUS.md §4.3): one probe, sent or unsent, produced by lib/wur/probes.py. One JSON object per line; validate line by line. raw_response is ALWAYS retained verbatim — every classifier above this line is re-derivable from it, which is what makes the D7 slot-classifier calibration recoverable without new runs. Attribution is by echoed probe_id, never by position.

slot.description: One of the three answer slots, annotated. Produced by protocol.annotate_slots(). With one fact per task (D1) at least 2 slots are filler by construction.

fact.description: Verbatim from the answer; the literal "NONE" when the model had fewer than 3 active facts.

affects_next_action.description: Null when the model did not supply a parseable boolean.

slot_class.description: HEURISTIC pending D7 (200 hand-labelled pilot slots). Precedence in protocol.classify_slot(): empty -> critical_fact -> distrusted -> task_restatement -> generic_workspace -> filler. `distrusted` means the slot reports the checkpoint mechanism itself or echoes the probe template — the failure the "Do not report facts about this checkpoint mechanism" clause exists to prevent (§6.2).

match_nonce.description: Mention tier (a): exact nonce, case-insensitive, whitespace-normalized (§4.5).

match_regex.description: Mention tier (b): a fact-specific paraphrase regex FROZEN IN facts.yaml BEFORE ANY DATA.

match_llm.description: Mention tier (c): 3-vote LLM adjudication. Null until adjudicated. Primary = (a) OR (b); tier (c) becomes primary only if kappa((a)v(b),(c)) < 0.6 — decided by kappa, not by which gives a nicer result.

matched_regex.description: The tier-(b) pattern that fired, for audit.

source_verified.description: The cited source resolves to a path that exists in the run's workspace. Null when not adjudicated.

wrong_value.description: d2-dist only: a distractor's token landed in this slot.

condition_id.description: Arm id, e.g. d2 or ctrl.

probe_idx.description: k — the index into probe_plan.json's fire_at.

echoed_probe_id.description: What the model echoed back. Differs from probe_id only on a superseded/confused answer; attribution follows this field.

sent_at_barrier.description: Realized barrier ordinal at injection. Rollup asserts that for a given (task_id, rep) all arms agree on the common prefix of this sequence, else probe_integrity: "schedule_divergence".

planned_at_barrier.description: probe_plan.json fire_at[probe_idx] — intended vs realized cadence.

raw_response.description: ALWAYS RETAINED VERBATIM — the model's full reply text for this probe turn, unmodified. Null only when nothing was ever received (outcome unanswered/superseded).

parse_tier.description: The parse ladder of protocol.parse_answer(): strict (exactly one ```json fence satisfying probe_answer.schema.json) -> lenient (any decodable object carrying `facts`, slots padded/truncated to 3) -> failed. STATUS.md §4.3 calls the middle rung "retry"; the re-ask is recorded separately in retry_sent/answered_after_retry so the tier always describes the PARSE, not the transport.

retry_sent.description: RETRY_TEXT was injected for this probe.

slots.description: Exactly 3 entries once anything parsed (protocol.parse_answer pads and truncates); empty when parse_ok is false.

next_action.description: The model's stated next move — the input to probe fidelity, compared against the actually-issued next tool call.

next_action_tool.description: The tool actually called next, for the fidelity comparison.

outcome.description: answered = a reply arrived for this probe_id. superseded = probe k+1 fired while k was pending; never suppress a probe, mark k superseded (§6.2). unanswered = sent, run ended first. refused = the reply reads as a refusal (protocol.looks_like_refusal). The pilot gate is refused == 0: a refusal means the trusted stream-json channel broke (V1/V2).

is_probe_turn_seq.description: events.jsonl seq values marked is_probe_turn for this probe.

kind.description: Resumes are counted separately from probes by lib/extract/core.py.

turn_message_ids.description: Assistant message.ids belonging to this probe's turns. Consumed by lib/extract/core.py to compute tool_calls_task (§4.4 difficulty band = tool calls EXCLUDING probe turns). Absent => core.py falls back to tool_calls_task == tool_calls_total, which is silently wrong on a probed run.

tool_use_ids.description: tool_use_ids issued inside this probe's turns; the second half of the tool_calls_task computation.

tokens_out.description: Output tokens spent on this answer — the instrument's own cost, measured (deduped by message_id).

allOf.description: A parsed answer always carries exactly three slots — the probe demands 3 entries and the parser pads to 3.
An answered probe has a reply on disk.
